keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Kasanje): the page says the band 'settled his followers on the upper Kwango River' and that by the 1650s conquests had given it six languages; no area or boundary is given. Drawn as the Kwango corridor of Malanje Province (confidence low).

region.text: the upper Kwango River, 'the Baixa de Cassange region of modern Angola along the Kwango River'

ledger.note: 1620: an Imbangala band that had deserted the Portuguese founds Kasanje on the upper Kwango. 'It was formed in 1620 by a mercenary band of Imbangala, which had deserted the Portuguese ranks.' The Imbangala page confirms the settlement 'in the Baixa de Cassange region of modern Angola along the Kwango River' but gives no founding date.

region.text: Bembe, 'significant taking of areas in Bembe in 1657', on the Angolan side of the Kwango

ledger.note: 1657: Kasanje takes areas in Bembe. 'The conquests continued in this decade with significant taking of areas in Bembe in 1657.' The page does not locate Bembe; the Kwango corridor widened is the reading (confidence 1). fx-32 (F199): region cut to Angola. The Kingdom of Kasanje page (opened 2026-11-01): 'Kasanje is located on the upper Kwango River in what is now Angola'; it names no land in the present Democratic Republic of the Congo and does not say where Bembe lies. The bare 120 km river buffer had run 479 cells into the DRC's Kwango and Kwilu (the Congo Free State's own land from 1885, 418 cells in the conflict list); the Angolan 550 cells are kept as the original reading of the takings in Bembe (confidence low).

wars.note: The page gives no date for the Matamba conflict; 1650 is the 'by the 1650s' marker. Matamba page dates: 1634-1635, 1681, 1683.

notes: Cliopatria has no Kasanje. The page gives no area; the shape is a proxy (Malanje Province within 80 km of the Kwango) and the capital is approximate (gazetteer Malanje). End year: the lead says 1910, the body 1910-1911, the infobox 1911-1912. Not settled: the Kasanje-Lunda tribute relation (not on either page), the Portuguese fort Cassange and any 18th-century treaty, Bembe's location, king list (the table is missing from the page). Page budget (2-5): three pages. | fx-32 F199: ledger[1] (1657 Bembe) is now the 120 km Kwango buffer inside Angola only; the keyframe (Malanje intersect 80 km of the Kwango) was already Angolan, so the Free State overlap came from this event alone.
